subject: Civic Education
competence: Works as a good citizen in a democratic society
lesson: Expresses the fact that the democratic life style brings out the well-being of the society: Grama Niladhari Public Benefit Inquiry
unique_learning_outcome: Expresses the fact that the democratic life style brings out the well-being of the society.
the_entrance: 5-minute introduction: The teacher enters the classroom holding two contrasting local newspaper headlines from a suburban Sri Lankan Pradeshiya Sabha area—one describing a community water project successfully resolved via village shramadana and open discussion, and another showing stalled development due to autocratic decision-making. Walking among the 7 student teams, the teacher poses a sharp opening question: 'When local leaders ignore public consultation, what happens to our community harmony and public welfare?' Students turn to their table partners for a rapid 60-second pair-share. The teacher prompts two students to voice their thoughts, immediately linking everyday citizen experiences to how democratic lifestyles directly guarantee societal well-being and equitable public services.

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: The teacher distributes mock citizen feedback reports detailing infrastructure decisions made democratically versus non-democratically in a suburban Sri Lankan division. Acting strictly as a facilitator, the teacher circulates among the 7 teams, prompting group leaders to ensure every member examines the data on resource allocation, public satisfaction, and conflict levels.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Student teams consisting of 5 members assign internal roles (Leader, Scribe, Timekeeper, Spokesperson, Civic Investigator) and review the citizen feedback data written on the chalkboard and supplied sheets. The Scribe records initial welfare indicators in student notebooks while the Civic Investigator cross-checks the data against textbook concepts of societal well-being.
lesson_development_steps.learning_teaching_aids: Chalkboard, Student Notebooks, Mock Citizen Feedback Reports

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: The teacher moves dynamically from group to group, asking probing questions such as 'How does respecting minority representation in this case study prevent community conflicts?' The teacher scaffolds student discussions on minority rights, majority consensus, and lawful living, encouraging teams to ground their analysis in the official textbook principles.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Students actively collaborate around chart papers to construct an evidence-backed impact diagram linking democratic lifestyle pillars (cooperation, transparency, equality) to community welfare indicators like minimized conflicts and satisfied public needs. Team members debate points respectfully, with the Timekeeper monitoring pacing and the Spokesperson drafting the presentation layout.
lesson_development_steps.learning_teaching_aids: Chart Paper, Colored Markers, Textbook Reference Pages

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: The teacher acts as a moderator for group presentations, inviting spokespersons to share their impact diagrams in a structured rotation. The teacher guides peer evaluation by asking the rest of the class to identify common threads across different group findings and consolidates core syllabus takeaways on democratic social well-being.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Each team's Spokesperson presents their diagram to the class, explaining how democratic practices foster peaceful, law-abiding societies in Sri Lanka. Peer students from listening teams use evaluation checklists to assess the presentations, while the Scribes update their notebooks with synthesized insights from other groups.
lesson_development_steps.learning_teaching_aids: Chart Paper Posters, Whiteboard, Peer Evaluation Checklists

summary: In this 2-minute synthesis, the teacher reviews how democratic lifestyles—such as working cooperatively, respecting minority and majority opinions, and ensuring transparency—directly establish harmonious, peaceful, and law-abiding societies across Sri Lankan communities.
assessment_and_feedback_whole_lesson: Formative assessment is conducted through continuous observation of group collaboration, evaluation of the completed impact diagrams for factual accuracy against textbook concepts, and structured peer feedback during presentations.
post_activity: To conclude actively in 5 minutes, each student writes down one concrete daily habit of democracy that promotes societal well-being on an exit slip and drops it into the classroom 'Democracy Box' on the teacher's desk as they exit.
selected_activity:
Activity: Grama Niladhari Public Benefit Inquiry
Approach: Student teams examine mock citizen feedback reports from a suburban Sri Lankan Pradeshiya Sabha area to evaluate how inclusive, democratic lifestyle practices yield societal welfare and equitable public services.
Student task: Teams review specific evidence data written on the chalkboard detailing infrastructure decisions made democratically versus non-democratically, recording welfare indicators in their notebooks.
Teacher facilitation: Teacher acts as a resource guide, prompting students to examine how citizens' voices improve public welfare and monitoring group role rotation to ensure full participation.
Expected output: An evidence-backed impact diagram on chart paper linking democratic lifestyle pillars to community welfare.
Grouping: 7 teams (7 groups of 5) with assigned roles: Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer. All 35 students engage actively through structured role distribution.
